observation_summary: The Complex.add() method failed to return NaN when one of the operands was NaN, violating the documented contract and causing assertion failures in tests.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves adding a conditional check (if (isNaN || rhs.isNaN)) at the beginning of the add() method to validate the input parameters and return the correct result (NaN) when appropriate. This is a classic missing guard/validation check.
evidence_used: The bug report states: 'Subtract includes an isNaN test and returns Complex.NaN if either complex argument isNaN; but add omits this test.'
The fix_diff_oracle shows the addition of an 'if (isNaN || rhs.isNaN) { return NaN; }' block at the start of the add() method.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the logic was technically incorrect, the root cause is the absence of a guard condition to handle the NaN case, which is specifically categorized as Checking.
